gemma4:12b.notes: auroc_drift_vs_nondrift: AUROC of score_for_drift = (1 - confidence) predicting label == 'drift' (positive) against ALL non-drift rows (faithful + degraded pooled as negative). This is the reviewer's direct ask -- distinct from auroc_faithful_vs_rest, which tests faithful vs. {degraded OR drift} and so does not isolate drift specifically. AUROC > 0.5 means lower stated confidence is associated with drift. auroc_faithful_vs_rest / ece_faithful_vs_rest reproduce the existing manuscript framing (idrift.analysis.calibration_v2.ece) bit for bit, reported alongside for direct contrast. brier / calib_intercept / calib_slope are the Brier score and Cox logistic recalibration (intercept, slope) of the SAME score_for_drift against the observed label == 'drift' indicator; intercept 0 and slope 1 would indicate perfect calibration of that drift-risk proxy. drift_fnr_at_threshold[t] = P(confidence >= t | label == 'drift'): the fraction of true drift outputs a 'confidence < t flags for review' rule would MISS.

pooled.pooled_note: POOLED ACROSS MODELS: verbalized confidence is not on a comparable scale across models -- an '80% confident' statement from one model is not the same probability claim as from another (see idrift.analysis.calibration_v2 module docstring). This block pools raw confidence across every model's rows for descriptive context only; it is NOT a claim that models share one confidence scale. Report per-model numbers (per_model) as primary.
